newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Tung working out fate of US$19 bln Land Fund.
newsitem.headline: HK's Tung working out fate of US$19 bln Land Fund.

text.p: Hong Kong's future leader Tung Chee-hwa will decide soon on arrangements for managing the territory's cash mountain earned from government land sales, a spokesman for Tung told Reuters on Wednesday.
"They will be announced pretty soon, could be very soon," spokesman Bob Howlett said.

The HK$150 billion (US$19.38 billion) Land Fund, created in 1983 to hold half of the revenues from government land sales, will be turned over to Hong Kong's post-handover government after the British colony reverts to Chinese rule on July 1.
Howlett also confirmed Tung is considering some arrangements outlined in two local newspapers.
The Hong Kong Economic Journal said Tung has decided the Land Fund would be independently operated as part of the Exchange Fund, the reserves used to back the local dollar.
It said the Land Fund would come under the supervision of Joseph Yam, chief executive of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA), the de facto central bank.
"Everything mentioned in the Economic Journal is (being considered)," Howlett said.
Hong Kong officials, including Yam and Financial Secretary Donald Tsang, have argued the Land Fund should be managed along with the Exchange Fund, which stood at HK$534.5 billion at the end of 1996.
The Land Fund's chief executive Chung Shui-ming would leave but all other managerial staff would remain, the newspaper said.
The daily Ming Pao said Tung proposed that the Land Fund operate independently and not be merged with the Exchange Fund.

After July 1, Tung would receive the fund on behalf of the post-colonial government and present it to Tsang's office, Ming Pao said. Tsang which would then hand it to Yam at the HKMA, who would coordinate its investments and management, it said.
But Ming Pao said the proposal might not go ahead because of objections from some members of Tung's cabinet.
